items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: My mother's father's name was Isadore John Barbarin.

ctx.x: Well, what was your mother's parent's name?

My mother's father's name was Isadore John Barbarin. His wife, his maiden name was Josephine Auphidore(?). Her grandmother's mother had came from Haiti. She spoke French, she spoke Creole, she spoke Patois and Cajol(?). All of them is different versions of the French, all of them spoke by different people. French was spoken by the Whites. Cajol(?) was spoken by the White Cajuns who were living in the country -- from the Acadians. There was

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Isidore Barbarin. And he walked at home, and we listened.

ctx.x: Isidore Barbarin. And he walked at home, and we listened. He used to play a little melody or something, and he’s watching. He’s pacing hisself, because you can get rusty. You get out of the pace, you get out of the pace of the rhythm that you’re playing, because them bands march at a certain tempo and a certain pace, and that’s what he practiced.

items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: since my father met my mother. He was Rose Barbera. He was a daughter of Isidot Barbera. A member of the original Longwood Brass Band.

ctx.x: Now where did you say he came from, Ball?

Ball came from Kentucky. Kentucky. It's a mystery to me how he came down south. He was going north. I think he was employed on one of the river boats. He settled in New Iberia. That's why I met my grandmother. He was born with four children. He moved in the Walther. And he worked as a stevedo, a long shaman on the river front.
